paraphrase: Paippalāda asks what arose first; the Lord answers: Sadyojāta, Aghora, Vāmadeva, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna — the five Brahmans — correspond to elements, Vedas and powers; all is Śiva.

checks.note: The prose question of Paippalāda and the five Brahmans (Sadyojāta … Īśāna) come before v. 1. Vv. 1-10 map them onto elements, Vedas, fires and powers (sadyojātaṃ mahī pūṣā …; ṛgvedo gārhapatyaṃ … kriyā śaktiḥ). The prose itself has no numbers.

paraphrase: Addressed to Śākala: Śiva dwells in the cave of the heart; the five-syllable mantra; knowing the five Brahmans one is liberated.

checks.note: The e-text has only 36 numbered verses after the prose. The address to Śākala comes just before v. 1. The pañcākṣara is at v. 24; the dahara, the heart-cave where Śiva is to be sought, is at vv. 34-36; the text ends at v. 36 'ityupaniṣat'.
